description:
As an audience analyst
  I want daily audience rows aggregated over a date range by channel, genre or day
  So that I can report reach and engagement for a period without summing raw rows myself

  Expected aggregates are recomputed from api/data/audience.json, programmes.json and
  channels.json: totalViewers is an exact sum, the two averages are plain arithmetic means over the
  matched daily rows (checked to within the API's documented rounding), programmes counts distinct
  programmes and meta.rows is the number of daily rows that fell inside the filter. The fixture
  covers 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31 and has rows on both of those boundary days.

description:
As an API consumer and as the operator who reads its logs
  I want every response, successful or not, to follow the same HTTP conventions
  So that clients can handle errors uniformly and a request can be traced end to end

  This feature deliberately works at the HTTP level (raw paths and methods) because the
  behaviour under test is the surface itself: read-only routes answer 405 with an Allow header
  (OPTIONS included, as CORS preflight is out of scope), HEAD is served with GET semantics,
  unknown routes answer 404 with the standard envelope, every response is JSON with a request id,
  and hostile input never produces a 5xx or reflected markup.

the response should carry a request id header

  code VALIDATION_ERROR, and lists every offending parameter in details[] so a client can fix a
  request in one round-trip. Numbers are coerced strictly: "1.5", "abc" and "" are not integers.

description:
As a payments analyst
  I want to find money that leaves an account and comes straight back
  So that quick round trips and payment reversals can be reviewed

  A round trip is a transfer A -> B followed by a transfer B -> A that happens
  at the same instant or after it and no more than 24 hours later, for an amount
  within 10% of what A sent. Both limits are inclusive. Each pair is reported once,
  with the earlier transfer as the original; when both legs carry the identical
  txn_time the lower txn_id is the original. The scenarios run
  sql/queries/01_round_trip_transfers.sql against sql/seed.sql, whose cases are
  documented in sql/README.md.

name: EMI calculator page

description:
The loan is configured only through the sliders, the schedule start month is changed with the calendar
  widget, and the yearly payment bar chart is checked for visibility, bar count and tooltip values.
  Tooltip amounts are cross-checked against the payment schedule table for the same year.

elements.name: Validate the yearly payment bar chart for a 10 lakh personal loan

steps.name: I open the EMI calculator
I navigate to the "Personal Loan" tab
I set the loan amount to 1000000 using the slider
I set the interest rate to 12% using the slider
I set the loan tenure to 5 years using the slider
I change the schedule start month to January of next year
the bar chart should be visible
the bar chart should show 5 years of payments with 2 bars per year
the tooltip of a bar should show its year and amounts greater than zero
the tooltip amounts should match the payment schedule table for that year

name: EMI bar chart on the Personal Loan tab (Test Case 2)

description:
The EMI is recalculated independently in the test (EMI = P·r·(1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n − 1)) and compared with the
  figures the application displays. The pie chart's two sections (principal vs. total interest) must both be
  visible and greater than zero, and their percentages must agree with the independent calculation.

elements.name: Scenario A - validate the EMI and the payment break-up pie chart

steps.name: I open the EMI calculator
I navigate to the "Home Loan" tab
I enter a loan amount of 2500000, an interest rate of 10% and a tenure of 10 years
the displayed EMI should match the EMI calculated for the same inputs
the displayed total interest and total payment should match the calculated values
the pie chart should be visible
both sections of the pie chart should show values greater than zero
the pie chart sections should match the calculated principal and interest shares
